title: Pause before you buy
description: A 24-hour pause on non-essential buys can save more than any coupon.

body.heading: The wishlist trick
paragraphs: When you want something non-essential, add it to a wishlist with the date instead of buying it. If you still want it after 24 hours — or a week for bigger items — and it fits your budget, buy it with a clear head.
Many urges fade overnight. The item was often about the moment: boredom, stress, or a clever advert. A pause lets the moment pass and keeps your money for things that last.

body.heading: Ask three questions
paragraphs: Before buying, ask: Do I need it or just want it right now? Do I already own something similar? Where will it live? Honest answers stop a surprising number of purchases.
For online shopping, removing saved payment details adds a helpful bit of friction — you have to type the card number, which gives your brain time to catch up.

body.heading: Enjoy the saves
paragraphs: Add up what your pauses saved in a month. Seeing that number grow is its own reward, and you can move some of it to a goal you care about.

takeaway: Put non-essentials on a dated wishlist and let a 24-hour pause do the saving.
